assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology to incretin-based therapy is a coherent arc from basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, the incretin effect, insulinotropic action) to drugs that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. The impact on human health and on physiology is exceptional and clearly demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor and clinical translation) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide) form a defensible trio. Knudsen's industrial drug-design role and the Habener/Mojsov history are not among the credited names and credit among the early peptide discoverers is contested; I am relying on recall of the literature rather than verification.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by large independent randomized outcome trials and wide clinical use; the interpretation is stable and timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Allocation between peptide discoverers, physiologists and drug developers is contested.
Long-term safety and durability of the obesity indication are still accruing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed by chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, establishing a new therapeutic modality in cancer immunology. The concept, the costimulatory design and the clinical proof are all original and of lasting consequence.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CAR with costimulation, preclinical design), June (first durable clinical responses in CLL and costimulatory CAR clinical development) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cells) are the credited names that best map the decisive steps. Eshhar and others not on the list may deserve credit and are not available to me here.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and independent confirmation across centres; follow-up now exceeds a decade for early patients. Solid-tumour efficacy remains limited but does not undermine the prize-level discovery.
uncertainties: Credit for the original CAR concept versus clinical translation is divided and a person outside the credited list may be relevant.
Toxicity and secondary malignancy concerns are being monitored.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembling L1 virus-like particles that induce protective immunity produced the first vaccines to prevent cancer-causing infection, now with population-level evidence of reduced cervical precancer and cancer. The discovery is original, clear and of major public-health importance.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP vaccine concept and development) are a plausible trio; the early VLP work by other groups, including that of Zhou, is a possible competing claim that I cannot resolve from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of vaccination with national-registry evidence of effectiveness, independently reproduced.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be viewed as a vaccine and public-health recognition rather than a mechanistic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid synovium and that its blockade yields clinical benefit changed the treatment of RA and other inflammatory diseases and validated cytokine targeting in chronic autoimmunity. As a rheumatology-oriented physician-scientist I can judge the clinical consequence directly, but I weigh it on the same criteria as other candidates.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly carried out the decisive mechanistic and clinical studies; the credited pair is a clean allocation. Contributions from Kollias, Cerami/Tracey and antibody developers could be raised, but I treat them as outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of clinical use, multiple biologics and biosimilars and independent confirmation; the Lasker award has already recognized the work.
uncertainties: Whether the biologic-development contributions of others complicate the two-person attribution.
Prize might be seen as overlapping in spirit with the 2025 immune tolerance prize area, though the discoveries are distinct.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, from the ER-to-nucleus signalling through IRE1, HAC1 and its splicing to the mammalian pathways, defined a fundamental quality-control signalling system and links to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The conceptual novelty is high.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori elucidated the core signalling mechanism in yeast and mammals; the pairing is clean. Contributions from Kaufman, Ron and Shamu may be considered but the supplied credit is the pair.
assessment.maturity: Basic mechanism thoroughly confirmed over thirty years; therapeutic translation (for example ISRIB or IRE1 modulators) is still early, which does not diminish the basic discovery.
uncertainties: Credit relative to Ron, Kaufman and Sidrauski/Walter's ISR work that is not credited here.
Medical impact is largely indirect so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL turned CML from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. The impact is outstanding and the principle general.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development and translational leadership), Lydon (kinase inhibitor discovery programme) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) are the supplied names. Rowley and Nowell/Hungerford and Witte/Baltimore on the oncogene side sit upstream and are not on this list, which makes the allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with long-term survival data; it is arguably overdue and has already had Lasker recognition.
uncertainties: Upstream contributions to the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL oncogene biology are not credited.
Prior prize overlap with oncogene or targeted-therapy recognition is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, an effective treatment for a previously lethal infantile neurodegenerative disease, and proved the clinical viability of splice-switching oligonucleotide therapeutics. It is a clear, original and clinically impactful mechanism-to-drug story.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanisms and SMN2 exon 7 regulation underlying the ASO design) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are well matched. Others involved in SMN2 biology, such as Hua and Singh, might be raised, but the supplied credit is a workable pair.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of clinical follow-up and independent confirmation; the field is still evolving with gene therapy and small molecules.
uncertainties: Relative contribution of the academic mechanism versus drug-development work.
Long-term outcomes with newer competing SMA therapies are still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and interferon production, and has become central to understanding infection, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies, relevant to my own field), and anti-tumour immunity. It is a conceptually clear and original discovery.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP identification) and Barber and Ishikawa (STING identification) correspond to the decisive steps; the credit list also includes Wu and Sun, who are junior to Chen, so I limit the proposal to three.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistically well confirmed and widely reproduced, but therapeutic validation in humans has been limited so far, making the timing somewhat early compared with the other candidates.
uncertainties: Clinical translation of STING agonists and antagonists remains unproven.
Possible competing claims for the STING discovery and for the order of priority.
